Report standardized fit convergence diagnostics

Source: R/diagnostics.R
fit_diagnostics.Rd

Report standardized fit convergence diagnostics

Usage

fit_diagnostics(object)

Arguments

object

A fitted cdrgam model.

Value

A named list containing at least outcome, reasons, converged, code, and message. outcome is "success", "warning", or "nonconverged". A warning means that optimization converged but a recorded numerical or inferential diagnostic requires review. Custom backends also report available objective counts, gradient norms, boundary information, conditioning, and Hessian diagnostics. notes lists findings that do not change outcome. A sparse Gaussian REML fit adds a boundary_variance_components note when smoothing parameters are classified as on the boundary of their range; their profile bounds are in hessian_boundary. The optimizer_stopped_short reason means the reported optimum is not one: either a negative-curvature direction of the interior Hessian lies along a single smoothing parameter (listed in hessian_negative_directions), or, when the analytic Hessian was computed, a Newton step would still lower the -2 REML criterion by more than 0.1 (predicted_decrease). Negative curvature that mixes several smoothing parameters is reported as indefinite_outer_hessian. Such a fit also reports newton_step_max, the largest coordinate of that Newton step on the log smoothing-parameter scale, and predicted_decrease_floor, the smallest criterion change resolvable at the fitted criterion (1e-10 times its magnitude, at least 1e-8). A dense generalized block fit whose optimizer stalls on a flat criterion plateau counts as converged only when every gradient component of the -2 LAML criterion is below 0.01 and at least one log smoothing parameter exceeds 8 in absolute value; it then reports outcome "warning", the parameters in plateau, and the reason smoothing_parameter_plateau. gradient_norm is the largest gradient component over all smoothing parameters and exact_gradient_maximum the largest over the free ones. Along a well-curved direction either can exceed the gradient tolerance while the Newton step and predicted_decrease stay negligible; convergence is judged from predicted_decrease against predicted_decrease_floor.
